Welcome to Claverham Community College
I am delighted to welcome you to our College website, which offers an insight into the life, ethos, and achievements of our school.
At Claverham Community College, we provide students with a high-quality, broad, and ambitious education, enabling them to reach their full potential in a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment. Our curriculum, pastoral care, and enrichment programmes are designed to foster a love of learning, resilience, and personal responsibility, while promoting the College’s core values of Ambition, Integrity, Independence, Respect, and Resilience.
We are committed to developing students who, through determination and effort, achieve the highest levels of academic and personal development. Equally, we place great emphasis on consideration for others, polite and respectful behaviour, and positive contributions to our local and wider community. Our aim is to nurture responsible, community-minded, and globally aware young people who are prepared to shape the future.
Our success is underpinned by a distinct philosophy: high expectations, hard work, traditional values, strong relationships, and recognition of each individual’s worth. This approach has contributed to consistently strong academic outcomes and was recognised in our 2023 Ofsted inspection, where inspectors praised the college for pupils’ pride, resilience, and positive attitudes, as well as for the quality of leadership, collaboration, and staff engagement.
Claverham is more than a school. Our 42-acre campus is home to a recently opened state-of-the-art teaching wing, a vibrant Sports Centre, and Battle Day Nursery, all of which provide outstanding facilities that benefit both students and the wider community. We take pride in being at the heart of Battle and the surrounding villages, serving a diverse catchment and fostering strong connections with families and local organisations.
We hope you find our website helpful and informative. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you would like to learn more about the College, its values, or the opportunities available to our students and community.
Mr. P SwattonPrincipal.
Exam Results
The achievements of our students this year are a testament to their resilience, dedication, and hard work. As a College, we place great importance on the academic and personal growth of our students, and we are immensely proud of the accomplishments of this group of young adults.
Many of our students have delivered outstanding individual performances, including those who have earned the highest possible grades. Just as rewarding, however, has been celebrating the success of those who have made exceptional progress throughout their time at Claverham.
Our heartfelt congratulations go to all of the young people who have achieved such impressive results, which will undoubtedly serve as a foundation for their future success. These achievements reflect the commitment and dedication of both students and staff, as well as the unwavering support of parents and governors.
As always, we will continue to build on this success, striving to provide the excellent education that all of our students deserve.

Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Claverham Community College as the secondary school of choice for your child.
Claverham Community College accepts students in Years 7 to 11.
Choosing the right secondary school for your child is a big decision and we know that many parents who live in Battle and its surrounding area start actively exploring all available schools for their child at an early stage.
On this page we have included a number of documents which will hopefully help you with your decision-making process.
Each year we hold an open evening and a number of open mornings whereby prospective parents and students can see the college in operation.
In-year admissions (where a student is admitted part way through the academic year) are sometimes possible, but please be aware that Claverham Community College is generally oversubscribed in most year groups so it may, subject to circumstances, be necessary to join a waiting list.
For information on the availability of places for in-year admissions please contact Mrs Taylor. In-year admission applications are processed by East Sussex County Council.
If your child is due to join Year 7 in a secondary school in September 2026, you will need to apply by 31st October 2025.
To apply for a school place please use the link below;https://www.eastsussex.gov.uk/education-learning/schools/apply-for-a-school-place
What happens if you apply late
If you apply after the closing date, the request will be dealt with after all on-time preferences have been processed. This may affect your chances of securing a preferred school.
If you move into the area after the closing date you should apply for a school place as soon as possible. Please contact the East Sussex Admissions Team on;
Phone: 0300 33 09 472 between 10 am to 3 pm Monday to FridayEmail: admissions@eastsussex.gov.uk
What to expect
If you apply online, you will receive an email to confirm the admissions team received your application.
You can sign in to view your account at any time.
If you have sent a paper form it is your responsibility to check the admissions team have received this.
Offer of a place
Decisions are sent on the national offer day. We won’t give an early decision under any circumstances.
The Local Authority sends decisions on allocation day by email if you applied online, or by letter if not.
If you did not get the school(s) you wanted for your child, the decision letter will explain your options.
If you are successful in being offered a place at Claverham Community College we will be in touch shortly after the allocation date.

The Local Authorities Admissions team is responsible for our waiting list.

Pupil Absence
It is a legal requirement to inform the College if a pupil is going to be absent or will be arriving late for any reason (medical, interview etc.). Without an e-mail or use of Arbor our staff would have no way of knowing whether an absence was due to your child not being sent to school or being sent and not arriving.
REPORTING A CHILD’S ABSENCE OR LATE ARRIVAL
If your child is unwell or going to be late into school for any reason, for their safety, please contact the school before 08:30.
Absences need to be reported daily by email or through the Arbor parent app. Medical evidence can be requested at any time. This evidence could be in the form of a compliment slip, appointment card, copy of prescription, prescribed medicinal packaging or a doctor’s note. Parents can be fined by ESCC if medical evidence is not provided.
All pupils who arrive late to school or need to leave early for any reason must report to Reception to sign in, or out, as appropriate.
If your child returns to school after an illness and you would like to inform us that your child has been sent, please contact the College using the above contact details so that we can alert you if your child does not arrive at school as expected. Please contact us again on Monday morning if your child’s illness continues into a second week.
For the latest guidance on Covid-19 please check the Government website here here
Medical Appointments
I would ask parents to give the College advanced notice of medical appointments where these cannot be arranged outside school hours. If a medical appointment requires your child to leave during the school day a letter from you is still required and needs to be handed to your child’s House Tutor for signature at morning registration on the day of the appointment, this letter needs to be handed to reception when signing out as confirmation that they have permission to leave. I understand it is not always possible to make medical appointments out of school hours but appreciate your efforts in keeping the amount of missed time to a minimum.
The Department for Education (DfE) has amended the regulations and guidance in relation to absences in term-time. There is no automatic right to take your child out of school during term time. From 1st September 2013, government legislation no longer enables head teachers to authorise requests for leave for children to be taken out of school unless there are considered to be exceptional circumstances.
